reader.requirement: At --std 85 a COMPUTE whose arithmetic expression is a single numeric identifier, a numeric literal or the figurative ZERO must set each identifier-1 (numeric or numeric edited) to that value under the MOVE-like alignment of the arithmetic statements (absolute value into an unsigned receiver, truncation or ROUNDED at the receiver, editing, P-scaled receivers); a nonnumeric literal, alphanumeric or group identifier, or other figurative constant is not an arithmetic expression and must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal: an unphrased size error at 85 continues to the next statement
OPTIONS inert below 2002, so the NATIVE arithmetic default holds
GateBooleanOperators introduction-gates the 2002+ boolean COMPUTE format; not reached by a numeric single operand

reader.edition-search: grep for DialectBehavior|DialectLevel|Edition in ArithmeticEmitter.cs and NumericRenderer.cs, and for computeStatement in CobolParserCore.g4 (one grammar rule for every edition, F2 gated in VersionConformancePass).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the stored value is the same at 85 and 2023; only an unphrased size error's disposition differs
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf02_02 covers an identifier and literals into numeric, edited and sign-separate receivers; not exercised: negative into unsigned, high-order truncation, the 18-digit maximum, P-scaled sender and receiver, ZERO, an ODO-table element, a FUNCTION identifier, a size error on the single value, and the refusal half

probes.expected: absolute value -123.45 into 9(3)V99 = 123.45; into S99V9 high-order truncated -23.4; 1599 into 99PP truncates to 1500; 9PP 500 -> 500.00; edited $123.45-; ZERO -> +0000; FUNCTION INTEGER(12.7) = 12; -0.05 into S99V9 truncates to zero
the largest 18-digit literal stored whole; 123 into PIC 99 without the phrase leaves an undefined value (23 shown) and continues; with ON SIZE ERROR the receiver is unchanged (23) and the phrase runs

probes.printed: G8 3.3 (COMPUTE RT = TE (N), TE OCCURS 1 TO 5 DEPENDING ON N, N = 3)
refused (exit 65): "12" COBOL1511 boolean-operand messages; X COBOL0844 alphanumeric not a numeric operand; group G COBOL0844; SPACE and ALL "1" COBOL1511; alphanumeric receiver X COBOL1675
probes.expected: each refused: not an arithmetic expression (§1985:VI.2 arithmetic expression definition) or not a numeric/numeric-edited identifier-1 (§1985:VI.6.8.3 SR1)

probes.printed: COMPUTE R EQUAL 5: error COBOL0001 cannot parse construct near 'EQUAL'

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.8.4 GR1  (║6.8.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: A single operand renders through FieldNum or LiteralNum and lands once through StoreArith with the receiver's truncation, ROUNDED and editing; every probe matched the text. Side observation outside this rule: at 85 a nonnumeric literal, SPACE or ALL literal right of = is refused with COBOL1511 messages that cite the 2023 boolean COMPUTE format (§2023:14.9.8.3 Format 2 SR2), a format 1985 does not have; the refusal is right, the diagnosis points at a non-1985 construct.

refuter.evidence: Class c, 1985 operand class: rcbad.cob COMPUTE R1 = E1 with E1 PIC ZZ9.99 is refused COBOL0844 at 85, as §1985:VI.6.2.1 requires (identifiers must be numeric elementary items); rcflt.cob COMPUTE R1 = 1.5E2 refused COBOL0900 (floating-point literal requires 2002). rcomp.cob (rcomp-001): COMPUTE R3 = ZEROES -> 000 (the ZEROES spelling of the 1985 figurative); COMPUTE MX = 9(18) max -> 999999999999999999; COMPUTE RP ROUNDED = 1549 into 99PP -> 1500; COMPUTE SP = .0007 into SVPP9 -> 0 and SR = SP -> 0.000; COMPUTE BN = 12345 into 9(4) BINARY -> SIZE, unchanged 0000, and 9999 stored; -12.5 into an unsigned receiver -> 012. All match the text. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.8.4 GR1 the text is in GR1; OK §1985:VI.6.2.1 the text is in the clause.
